discover.intro: Ratios compare quantities by multiplication. Most "how many" problems in contests are ratio problems in disguise.

problem.q: A smoothie recipe uses strawberries and bananas in the ratio 5 : 3. You want 24 pieces of fruit total. How many strawberries do you need?
problem.sol: 5 : 3 means 8 equal "parts" of fruit: 5 parts strawberry, 3 parts banana. 24 pieces in 8 parts is 3 per part, so $5\cdot 3 = 15$ strawberries.

sections.md: The key was "parts": a ratio $5:3$ means the amounts are $5k$ and $3k$ for some number $k$. Once you find $k$ (here 3), everything else follows.
**A ratio $a : b$ means the quantities are $ak$ and $bk$ for some $k$.** Ratios can be scaled: $5 : 3 = 10 : 6 = 15 : 9$. Three-way ratios work the same way: $2 : 3 : 4$ means $2k, 3k, 4k$.

sections.title: Proportions
sections.problem: If 7 notebooks cost \$9.80, how much do 12 cost?

sections.md:
### Unit conversions
Multiply by fractions equal to 1, chosen so the unwanted units cancel:
$$3\text{ yd}\cdot\frac{3\text{ ft}}{1\text{ yd}}\cdot\frac{12\text{ in}}{1\text{ ft}} = 108\text{ in}.$$
**Careful with area and volume:** a square foot is $12\times 12 = 144$ square inches, not 12.

item.q: How many square feet are in 3 square yards?
item.sol: 1 square yard = $3\times 3 = 9$ square feet; times 3 is 27.

mis.9: That converts yards to feet once; area needs it twice: 3 × 3 = 9 sq ft per sq yd.

sections.title: A ratio that changes
sections.problem: A jar has red and blue marbles in ratio 3 : 4. After 10 red marbles are added, the ratio becomes 1 : 1. How many marbles were there originally?

steps.md: Originally $3k$ red and $4k$ blue. After: $3k + 10$ red, $4k$ blue.

steps.ask: Why can't you just use the numbers 3 and 4 directly?
steps.why: The ratio says *proportion*, not count: 3 : 4 could be 3 and 4, or 30 and 40. The multiplier $k$ captures the actual size.

sections.md: Rowan said: "The ratio of boys to girls is 2 : 3, so $\frac23$ of the class is boys."
sections.question: Is that right?
options: No: 2/5 of the class is boys
No: 3/5 of the class is boys
sections.explain: 2 : 3 means 5 equal parts, 2 of which are boys: $\frac25$ of the class. $\frac23$ is boys *compared to girls*, not compared to the whole class.

sections.prompt: A map scale says 1 cm : 5 km. Explain why an area of 1 square cm on the map is 25 square km, not 5.
sections.model: A 1 cm by 1 cm square on the map is a 5 km by 5 km square in real life, so its area is $5\times 5 = 25$ square km. Lengths scale by 5, so areas scale by $5^2$.

item.q: Ages of three siblings are in the ratio $2 : 3 : 5$ and add to 40. How old is the oldest?
item.sol: 10 parts make 40, so 4 per part; oldest $5\cdot 4 = 20$.

summary: Ratio $a : b$ means amounts $ak$ and $bk$. Find $k$ and you're done.
Convert units by multiplying by 1 in disguise; area units convert by the square, volume by the cube.

items.q: How many cubic feet are in 2 cubic yards?
items.sol: 1 cubic yard = $3^3 = 27$ cubic feet; times 2 is 54.

items.q: If $a : b = 2 : 3$ and $b : c = 4 : 5$, what is $a : c$? Give $\frac ac$ as a fraction.
items.sol: Make $b$ match: $a : b = 8 : 12$ and $b : c = 12 : 15$. So $a : c = 8 : 15$.
hints: Rescale both ratios so the $b$ values are equal.

items.q: A punch is 1 part juice to 4 parts soda. How much juice must be added to 10 liters of this punch to make it 1 part juice to 1 part soda?
items.sol: 10 L has 2 L juice and 8 L soda. To make juice equal soda, add 6 L of juice.

items.q: The ratio of the areas of two squares is $9 : 25$. What is the ratio of their perimeters? Give the smaller-to-larger ratio as a fraction.
items.sol: Areas scale as the square of side lengths, so sides are in ratio $3 : 5$, and perimeters (4 × side) are too.

reteach.md: **Another way: draw bars.** For $5 : 3$, draw 5 equal boxes in one bar and 3 equal boxes in another. If you know the total (24), divide it by all 8 boxes to find one box (3). Then read off whatever you need. This "tape diagram" is just $k$ drawn as a box.
Ratio problems: find the value of one part.

cards.front: What does the ratio $a : b$ mean in terms of actual amounts?
cards.back: The amounts are $ak$ and $bk$ for some positive number $k$.
